correctness.rationale: Radial wavefront counting for an edge-interior source starts with two tips; crossing a vertex changes the count by degree(v)−2. Integrating vertex ball lengths and Fubini gives the density in signed degree deficits, then the displayed CDF. For any cut edge, the sum of 2−degree over one separated component is exactly one, which controls signed pair-path edge monomials. Expanding path distances gives S1=2L, S2=2L², S3=2L³−12B; the noncollinear triple-edge terms have unique median branch. A finite-distance Laplace transform yields E[D]=S3/(6L²). B>0 for every true branching vertex and zero for paths. Independently checked 30 exact rational CDF radii on a nonuniform three-arm star, as well as star mean 41/60, complementing the inspected all-tree source verifier. The infinite statement relies on wave counting/separator identities.

value.rationale: A complete exact all-radii probability distribution and cubic branch-sensitive mean are natural invariants for random points on metric trees; they quantify by how much branching lowers the interval’s mean and identify sharp equality for arbitrary lengths.

final_claim: For every finite positive-length metric tree, the uniform-arclength pair-distance CDF is an explicit signed quadratic spline with vertex degree-deficit coefficients, and mean L/3−2B(T)/L² with sharp equality only for paths.
limitations: Finite acyclic connected trees, positive real lengths and uniform arclength sampling only.
Signed density knots may cancel; no inverse injectivity or stability claim.
